question: Check count-only evidence coverage for daridorexant in pregnancy across PubMed, ClinicalTrials.gov, DailyMed, LactMed and MPRINT. Explain what each count does and does not establish.
criteria: Use count-only probes. LactMed is lactation-only and not applicable to pregnancy. Do not equate counts or zero matches with evidence quality or safety. Preserve unknown versus zero.
answer:
## Count-only coverage for daridorexant in pregnancy

The MCP returned counts only; no narrative findings were retrieved. The counts are not comparable across sources and do not establish evidence quality, clinical safety, or what any study found. Zero matches may reflect query, indexing, snapshot, or population limits. [S4](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/)

| Source | Returned count/status | What the count establishes | What it does not establish |
|---|---:|---|---|
| **PubMed** | **3 matches** | Three records matched the returned daridorexant-and-pregnancy query. | The count does not establish verified human outcomes, distinct studies, or evidence quality. The query reported that the daridorexant MeSH phrase was not found. [S4](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/) |
| **ClinicalTrials.gov** | **4 matches** | Four registrations matched `daridorexant AND (pregnancy)`. | The count does not establish posted results, enrollment, outcomes, or confirmed age-band applicability. [S1](https://clinicaltrials.gov/) |
| **DailyMed** | **1 match** | One name-matched product label was returned. | The count does not establish population-specific sections, current FDA approval, or independent evidence. [S2](https://dailymed.nlm.nih.gov/) |
| **LactMed** | **Not applicable; no count** | LactMed was not used for this pregnancy count because it is lactation-only. | It does not provide pregnancy or general pediatric evidence. |
| **MPRINT Gold snapshot** | **0 literal drug-name row matches; 0 distinct PMIDs** | No literal daridorexant match was found in the selected MPRINT Gold snapshot tables. Snapshot date: **November 17, 2026**. | This does not establish that no relevant evidence exists elsewhere. The MCP reports that the lookup used literal drug-name row matching in selected snapshot tables, without name resolution or full portals; rows are not distinct studies. [S3](https://github.com/langli-lab/mprint-kp-data) |

This was a bounded, count-only lookup, not full evidence retrieval. The MCP states that its pregnancy coverage review did not identify a curated federal pregnancy counterpart to LactMed; that is a source-review finding, not proof that no such resource exists. [S6](https://www.fda.gov/drugs/labeling/questions-and-answers-pregnancy-and-lactation-labeling-rule) [S7](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK501922/)
